name: Sagrada Família
description: Antoni Gaudí’s unfinished basilica rises with sculpted towers over Eixample. Inside, coloured light filters through tall stained-glass windows.

name: Alhambra
description: A Nasrid palace-fortress crowns a hill above Granada. Courtyards, carved stucco and reflecting pools reward a slow walk.

name: Museo del Prado
description: Spain’s great art museum faces the Paseo del Prado. Rooms of Velázquez, Goya and more fill a neoclassical block.

name: Mosque-Cathedral of Córdoba
description: A forest of striped arches fills the former Great Mosque, later a cathedral. The dual history is visible in one continuous floor.

name: Park Güell
description: Gaudí’s park spreads mosaic benches and stone colonnades over a Carmel hillside. City and sea views open from the terrace.

name: El Retiro
description: Madrid’s central park holds a boating lake, formal gardens and the Crystal Palace. Locals walk, row and picnic between the avenues.

name: Plaza Mayor
description: An arcaded square anchors old Madrid with uniform façades and café terraces. Street life fills the centre from morning onward.

name: La Rambla
description: Barcelona’s tree-lined promenade runs from Plaça de Catalunya toward the waterfront. Flower stalls and side streets keep it busy.

name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
description: Frank Gehry’s titanium curves sit on the Nervión riverside. The building itself is as much a draw as the collection inside.

name: Toledo Old Town
description: Winding lanes climb a hill ringed by the Tagus. Churches, synagogues and workshops share the compact historic core.

name: La Boqueria
description: Barcelona’s covered market opens off La Rambla with seafood, fruit and tapas counters. Arrive early for the fullest stalls.

name: Mercado de San Miguel
description: A glass-and-iron food hall beside Plaza Mayor serves pintxos, oysters and wine by the glass. Stand at the counters and share plates.

name: Central Market of Valencia
description: A large modernist market hall fills with produce and seafood. Look for local oranges and rice ingredients used in paella.

name: Parte Vieja pintxos
description: San Sebastián’s Old Town is lined with bars of Basque pintxos. Hop between counters for small bites and txakoli.

name: Mercado de San Antón
description: A multi-level Chueca market mixes grocery stalls with ready-to-eat counters upstairs. Good for a casual lunch overlooking the square.

name: Feria de Abril
description: Seville’s April Fair fills fairground casetas with flamenco dress, horse parades and late-night dancing after Holy Week.
